# Setup

Notebook r1.01 shows each source as its own line.
This notebook fits one model to all of them, to put the four sources on one scale and to read a trend through noisy, unevenly spaced surveys.
The model is **descriptive**: it has no substantive predictors, only country, time and source.
Its output is a set of type shares per country and year *as the ESS would have measured them*, with posterior uncertainty, next to the raw cells of r1.01.

**Fit switch.** `full_fit <- TRUE` fits with 4 chains of 2,000 iterations (1,000 warm-up) and caches the fit in `data/04_models/` (git-ignored).
`full_fit <- FALSE` fits with 2 chains of 400 iterations and saves nothing; those estimates only show that the pipeline runs.
With `refit_allowed <- FALSE`, an existing cached fit is loaded and never refitted, even if the data changed; set it to `TRUE` to refit.

```{r}
#| label: setup

# To track render duration
start_time <- Sys.time()

# set width of console output
options(width = 80)

# Install and load required packages
p_required <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "here",
  "arrow",
  "brms",
  "cmdstanr",
  "posterior",
  "sessioninfo"
)
packages <- rownames(installed.packages())
p_to_install <- p_required[!(p_required %in% packages)]
if (length(p_to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(p_to_install)
}
sapply(p_required, require, character.only = TRUE)
rm(p_required, p_to_install, packages)

# Shared tree helpers: countries_25, ctype_levels
source(here("code", "00_helper", "pid_tree.R"))

# Fit settings
full_fit <- FALSE
refit_allowed <- FALSE
settings <- if (full_fit) {
  list(chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000)
} else {
  list(chains = 2, iter = 400, warmup = 200)
}
model_dir <- here("data", "04_models")
if (full_fit) dir.create(model_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Reference source and year for predictions
ref_source <- "ESS"
```

# Data

The input is the cell table of notebook r1.01: one row per survey × country, with the weighted share of each type and the cell's Kish effective sample size.
The model needs counts.
So each cell enters with **effective counts**, the weighted shares times `n_eff`, rounded.
A cell then carries as much information as its weights allow, no more.

```{r}
#| label: data

cells <- read_parquet(here("data", "02_processed", "composition_cells.parquet"))

# Short column names per type; non-partisan first, the reference category
type_cols <- c(
  "non-partisan" = "nonpartisan",
  "explicit" = "explicit",
  "mismatched" = "mismatched",
  "denier" = "denier",
  "attached non-voter" = "attnonvoter"
)

d <- cells |>
  mutate(
    col = type_cols[as.character(ctype)],
    k_eff = round(share_w * n_eff)
  ) |>
  select(source, survey, country, year, n, n_eff, col, k_eff) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = k_eff) |>
  mutate(
    # The EES moved online, with the party list on screen, in 2019 (notebook
    # 2.02); its explicit shares jump with it (notebook r1.01), so the two modes
    # are separate instruments
    source = if_else(source == "EES", if_else(year >= 2019, "EES online", "EES interview"), as.character(source)),
    source = factor(source, levels = c(ref_source, setdiff(c("ESS", "EES interview", "EES online", "CSES", "EU25"), ref_source))),
    country = factor(country, levels = countries_25),
    cell = paste(survey, country),
    # Decades from 2010
    year_c = (year - 2010) / 10
  )

# Count matrix in the order of type_cols
d$y <- as.matrix(d[, unname(type_cols)])
d$total <- rowSums(d$y)

# Cells per source; total effective respondents
d |>
  summarise(cells = n(), n_eff = sum(total), .by = source)
```

# Model

$$
\mathbf{y}_c \sim \text{Multinomial}(N_c, \boldsymbol{\pi}_c), \qquad
\log \frac{\pi_{c,k}}{\pi_{c,\text{non-partisan}}} = \alpha_k + \beta_{k,\text{source}[c]} + f_k(t_c) + a_{k,j[c]} + b_{k,j[c]}\, t_c + u_{k,c}
$$

for cell $c$ (one survey in one country $j$, in year $t$) and type $k$, against non-partisans as the reference category.

- $\beta_{k,\text{source}}$: the **source offset**, the difference that wording, mode and the vote asked about make, common to all countries; the ESS is the reference.
  It is identified where two sources observe a country at about the same time (the overlap table in r1.01).
- $f_k(t)$: a smooth European trend (thin-plate spline, `k = 5`).
- $a_{k,j}$, $b_{k,j}$: each country's level and linear trend around the European one (correlated varying effects).
- $u_{k,c}$: a cell effect, for the variation between surveys beyond sampling error (house and fieldwork effects).

This is the first rung: country deviations from the European trend are linear.
Country-specific smooths come next if the posterior predictive checks show curvature the linear deviations miss.

```{r}
#| label: formula

f <- bf(
  y | trials(total) ~ source + s(year_c, k = 5) + (1 + year_c | country) + (1 | cell),
  family = multinomial()
)

# One set of priors per linear predictor
dpars <- paste0("mu", unname(type_cols)[-1])
priors <- map(dpars, \(dp) {
  c(
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept", dpar = dp),
    set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", dpar = dp),
    set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sd", dpar = dp),
    set_prior("exponential(2)", class = "sds", dpar = dp)
  )
}) |>
  reduce(c) |>
  c(set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor"))

priors
```

The priors are weakly informative on the log-odds scale: an intercept within about ±4 (shares from 2% to 98% of the non-partisan count), source offsets mostly within ±2, and standard deviations of the varying effects mostly below 1.
The prior predictive check below shows what they imply for the shares.

```{r}
#| label: fit-helper

fit_model <- function(name, sample_prior = "no") {
  path <- file.path(model_dir, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (full_fit && file.exists(path) && !refit_allowed) {
    return(readRDS(path))
  }
  brm(
    f,
    data = d,
    prior = priors,
    sample_prior = sample_prior,
    chains = settings$chains,
    iter = settings$iter,
    warmup = settings$warmup,
    cores = settings$chains,
    backend = "cmdstanr",
    seed = 20261110,
    refresh = 0,
    silent = 2,
    file = if (full_fit) file.path(model_dir, name),
    file_refit = if (refit_allowed) "on_change" else "never"
  )
}
```

## Prior Predictive Check

Type shares drawn from the priors alone, for the observed cells.
They should spread over the whole unit interval without piling up at 0 or 1.

```{r}
#| label: prior-fit

fit_prior <- fit_model("composition_m1_prior", sample_prior = "only")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-prior
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

prior_shares <- posterior_epred(fit_prior, ndraws = 200)
# draws x cells x types, divided by the cell total
prior_shares <- sweep(prior_shares, 2, d$total, "/")

dimnames(prior_shares)[[3]] |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(k) tibble(share = as.vector(prior_shares[, , k]))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "type") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#0072B2") +
  facet_wrap(vars(type), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Prior predictive type shares", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Fit

```{r}
#| label: fit

fit <- fit_model("composition_m1")

# Draws used for predictions
n_draws <- min(1000, ndraws(fit))

# Convergence
draws_summary <- summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
draws_summary |>
  summarise(
    max_rhat = max(rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_bulk = min(ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ess_tail = min(ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Divergent transitions
nuts_params(fit) |>
  filter(Parameter == "divergent__") |>
  summarise(divergent = sum(Value))
```

# Posterior Predictive Checks

For every cell, the observed weighted share of each type against the 90% interval of the shares the model predicts for that cell (cell effects included).
If the model fits, about 90% of the cells fall inside their interval, in every source and type.
A source whose coverage falls short is one the model treats too much like the others.

```{r}
#| label: ppc

pred <- posterior_predict(fit, ndraws = n_draws)
pred <- sweep(pred, 2, d$total, "/")

obs <- d$y / d$total

ppc <- map(seq_along(type_cols), \(k) {
  tibble(
    source = d$source,
    country = d$country,
    year = d$year,
    type = names(type_cols)[k],
    observed = obs[, k],
    lo = apply(pred[, , k], 2, quantile, 0.05),
    hi = apply(pred[, , k], 2, quantile, 0.95)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(inside = observed >= lo & observed <= hi)

# Coverage of the 90% intervals
ppc |>
  summarise(coverage = round(mean(inside), 2), cells = n(), .by = c(source, type)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = coverage) |>
  arrange(source)
```

# Trajectories

The fitted share of each type by country and year, **as the ESS would measure it** (source set to ESS, cell effects left out).
The line is the posterior median, the band the 90% interval.
The points are the raw weighted cells of notebook r1.01, by source; they sit off the line where their source measures differently, which is what the source offsets absorb.
Trajectories are drawn only over the years a country is observed by some source.

```{r}
#| label: trajectories

# Country-years within each country's observed range
grid <- d |>
  summarise(first = min(year), last = max(year), .by = country) |>
  mutate(year = map2(first, last, \(a, b) seq(a, b))) |>
  unnest(year) |>
  mutate(
    source = factor(ref_source, levels = levels(d$source)),
    year_c = (year - 2010) / 10,
    total = 1L
  )

epred <- posterior_epred(
  fit,
  newdata = grid,
  re_formula = ~ (1 + year_c | country),
  ndraws = n_draws
)

traj <- map(seq_along(type_cols), \(k) {
  grid |>
    select(country, year) |>
    mutate(
      type = names(type_cols)[k],
      median = apply(epred[, , k], 2, median),
      lo = apply(epred[, , k], 2, quantile, 0.05),
      hi = apply(epred[, , k], 2, quantile, 0.95)
    )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-helper

source_colours <- c(ESS = "#0072B2", EES = "#E69F00", CSES = "#009E73", EU25 = "#CC79A7")
source_shapes <- c(ESS = 16, EES = 17, CSES = 15, EU25 = 18)
# Offsets split the EES by mode
source_colours <- c(source_colours, "EES interview" = "#E69F00", "EES online" = "#E69F00")
source_shapes <- c(source_shapes, "EES interview" = 17, "EES online" = 2)

plot_fitted <- function(type) {
  raw <- cells |>
    filter(ctype == type) |>
    mutate(country = factor(country, levels = countries_25))
  traj |>
    filter(type == !!type) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = year)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
    geom_line(aes(y = median), linewidth = 0.6, colour = "grey20") +
    geom_point(
      data = raw,
      aes(y = share_w, colour = source, shape = source),
      size = 1.2,
      alpha = 0.7
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(country), ncol = 5, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = source_colours) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = source_shapes) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2000, 2010, 2020), labels = c("'00", "'10", "'20")) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1996, 2024)) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Fitted share:", type),
      subtitle = "Posterior median and 90% interval at the ESS measurement; points are raw weighted cells by source",
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      colour = NULL,
      shape = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}
```

# Change per Country

The posterior change in each type's share between a country's first and last observed year, at the ESS measurement, in percentage points, with 50% and 90% intervals.
Countries are sorted by the median change in the explicit share.
Countries observed over different spans are not directly comparable; the span is printed in the label.

```{r}
#| label: change

span <- d |>
  summarise(first = min(year), last = max(year), .by = country)

idx_first <- match(paste(span$country, span$first), paste(grid$country, grid$year))
idx_last <- match(paste(span$country, span$last), paste(grid$country, grid$year))

change <- map(seq_along(type_cols), \(k) {
  delta <- 100 * (epred[, idx_last, k] - epred[, idx_first, k])
  span |>
    mutate(
      type = names(type_cols)[k],
      median = apply(delta, 2, median),
      lo90 = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.05),
      hi90 = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.95),
      lo50 = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.25),
      hi50 = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.75),
      p_decline = colMeans(delta < 0)
    )
}) |>
  list_rbind()

country_order <- change |>
  filter(type == "explicit") |>
  arrange(median) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(country, " (", first, "-", last, ")"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-change
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7

change |>
  left_join(select(country_order, country, label), by = "country") |>
  mutate(
    label = factor(label, levels = country_order$label),
    type = factor(type, levels = names(type_cols)[c(2, 3, 4, 5, 1)])
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo90, xmax = hi90), linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#0072B2") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo50, xmax = hi50), linewidth = 1.4, colour = "#0072B2") +
  geom_point(aes(x = median), size = 1.6, colour = "#0072B2") +
  facet_wrap(vars(type), nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Change in type shares, first to last observed year",
    subtitle = "Percentage points at the ESS measurement; posterior median, 50% and 90% intervals",
    x = "Change (pp)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# Source Offsets

How the sources differ when they measure the same electorate.
The figure shows each type's share for a typical country (varying effects at zero) in 2014, as each source would measure it, minus the ESS share, in percentage points.

```{r}
#| label: offsets

offset_grid <- tibble(
  source = factor(levels(d$source), levels = levels(d$source)),
  year_c = 0.4,
  total = 1L
)

offset_epred <- posterior_epred(fit, newdata = offset_grid, re_formula = NA, ndraws = n_draws)

offsets <- map(seq_along(type_cols), \(k) {
  delta <- 100 * (offset_epred[, , k] - offset_epred[, 1, k])
  tibble(
    source = offset_grid$source,
    type = names(type_cols)[k],
    median = apply(delta, 2, median),
    lo = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.05),
    hi = apply(delta, 2, quantile, 0.95)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(source != ref_source)

offsets |>
  mutate(across(c(median, lo, hi), \(x) round(x, 1)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-offsets
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

offsets |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = names(type_cols)[c(2, 3, 4, 5, 1)])) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = source, x = median, colour = source, shape = source)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(vars(type), nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = source_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = source_shapes, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Source offsets against the ESS",
    subtitle = "Typical country, 2014; percentage points, posterior median and 90% interval",
    x = "Difference from ESS (pp)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# Save

The trajectories, changes and offsets (posterior summaries) and the draws of the change per country go to `data/05_results/composition_post.rds`, which slides and the manuscript read instead of the fit.
Only a full fit is saved.

```{r}
#| label: save

if (full_fit) {
  dir.create(here("data", "05_results"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  list(
    trajectories = traj,
    change = change,
    offsets = offsets,
    ppc_coverage = ppc |> summarise(coverage = mean(inside), .by = c(source, type)),
    diagnostics = draws_summary,
    settings = settings,
    reference = list(source = ref_source, offset_year = 2014)
  ) |>
    write_rds(here("data", "05_results", "composition_post.rds"))
}
```

# Caveats

- **The source offsets are assumed common to all countries.** Where a source measures differently in one country (a national wording, an odd sample), the difference lands in that country's cells and trend.
- **The offsets are identified only by overlaps.** Countries observed by one source alone take the offsets estimated elsewhere.
- **Linear country deviations.** A country whose trend bends differently from the European spline is smoothed toward a line; check the trajectories against the raw points.
- **Effective counts are rounded** weighted counts, an approximation to a weighted likelihood.
- **The model does not read causally.** It describes who reports which type; it does not separate age, period and cohort.
- **Development fits** (`full_fit <- FALSE`) are too short to interpret.
